Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 72, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Surat al-Jinn is Meccan, according to the consensus. It has twenty-eight verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened, and they said: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord. And exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has taken neither a consort nor a son."﴾

There are five issues in this.

The first: His saying, the Exalted: "Say: It has been revealed to me." That is, say, O Muhammad, to your community: Allah revealed to me through Jibril that a company of the jinn listened to me. He (ﷺ) did not know about it before it was revealed to him. This is what Ibn Abbas and others said, as will come. Ibn Abi Ablah read "uhiya" [[In the originals it is written (wahiya), and the correct reading is what we have established, which agrees with what appears in (Taj al-'Arus: wahy). It says: Juwaybir al-Asadi recited: (Qul uhiya ilayya), and it did not attribute the reading to Ibn Abi Ablah.]] according to the original form. It is said: awha ilayhi and wahaa, so the waw was changed into a hamza. From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered at their appointed time﴾ [al-Mursalat 77:11], and it is metathesis (qalb, the transposition of letters), whose permissibility is absolute in every waw that carries a damma. Al-Mazini also applied it absolutely to the waw with a kasra, as in ishah (for wishah, a sash), isadah (for wisadah, a support), and "i'a akhihi" (for wi'a akhihi, the "container of his brother") and similar forms.

The second: It has been disputed whether the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them or not. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that he did not see them, because of His saying "listened" and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when We turned to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:29]. In the Sahih of Muslim and al-Tirmidhi [[The wording is Muslim's; as for al-Tirmidhi, his wording contains an addition.]] from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recite to the jinn nor see them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with a group of his companions, intending Souq Ukaz, and the devils had been prevented from the news of the heaven, and shooting stars were sent against them. The devils returned to their people, and they said: "What is the matter with you?" They said: "We have been prevented from the news of the heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us!" They said: "Nothing but something new has happened. Strike the eastern and western parts of the earth and see what this is that has come between us and the news of the heaven." So they set off striking the eastern and western parts of the earth. The company that took the way toward Tihama, and he was at Nakhla [[So it is in (a), (h), (t), and it is the correct reading.]], intending Souq Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: "This is what has come between us and the news of the heaven." They returned to their people and said: "O our people, indeed we have heard a Qur'an that is wondrous [[In (h): "Indeed we have heard a book sent down after Musa, a Qur'an that is wondrous ..." etc.]], which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened﴾.

He related it from Ibn Abbas, who said: The saying of the jinn to their people, when "the servant of Allah stood calling upon Him, they nearly became a mass upon him" [al-Jinn 72:19], He said: When they saw him praying and his companions praying with his prayer, prostrating with his prostration. He said [[In (h): "and prostrating with him ..."]]: They marvelled at the obedience of his companions to him. They said to their people: "When the servant of Allah stood calling upon Him, they nearly became a mass upon him." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan and sahih. In this hadith there is evidence that he (ﷺ) did not see the jinn, but they attended him and heard his recitation. In it there is also evidence that the jinn were with the devils when they spied on the news, because of the devils, when they were struck by the shooting stars. And those struck by the shooting stars were also among the jinn. They were called devils, as He said: ﴿the devils of mankind and the jinn﴾ [al-An'am 6:112], for every rebellious one who departs from the obedience of Allah is a shaytan.

In al-Tirmidhi from Ibn Abbas, who said: The jinn used to ascend to the heaven to listen to the revelation. When they heard a word, they added nine to it. As for the word, it would be true, and as for what they added to it, it would be false. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, they were prevented from their seats. They mentioned that to Iblis, and shooting stars had not been thrown before that. Iblis said to them: "This matter is nothing but something that has happened on earth!" So he sent his soldiers, and they found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing praying between two mountains — I think he said in Mecca — so they came to him and informed him. He said: "This is the event that has happened on the earth." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan and sahih. This hadith indicates that the jinn were struck as the devils were struck.

In the narration of al-Suddi: When they were struck, they came to Iblis and informed him of what had happened to them. He said: "Bring me from every land a handful of dust that I may smell it." They brought it to him, and he smelled it and said: "Your companion is in Mecca." So he sent a company of the jinn — it is said they were seven, and it is said nine, among them Zawba'a. Zirr narrated from Asim: The company of Zawba'a and his companions came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Thumali said: They were from the Banu al-Shaysaban, who are the most numerous of the jinn and the strongest in power, and they are the general body of Iblis's soldiers. Asim also narrated from Zirr: They were seven men, three from the people of Harran and four from the people of Nasibin. Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: They were nine from the people of Nasibin (a village in Yemen, other than the one in Iraq) [[We did not find the Nasibin mentioned by the author in Mu'jam maAsta'jam by al-Bakri, nor in Mu'jam al-Buldan by Yaqut, nor in what the author of Taj al-'Arus quoted from Yaqut.]]. It was said: The jinn who came to Mecca were the jinn of Nasibin, and those who came to him at Nakhla were the jinn of Nineveh. The explanation of this has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf [[See vol. 16, p. 211.]]. Ikrima said: The surah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite was "Read in the name of your Lord" [al-'Alaq 96:1]. The explanation of the names of the company of the jinn has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf, so there is no point in repeating it.

It is said that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw the jinn on the night of the jinn, and this is more firmly established. Amir al-Sha'bi narrated: I asked Alqama, "Was Ibn Mas'ud present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?" Alqama said: "I asked Ibn Mas'ud, 'Was any of you present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?' He said: 'No, but we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night, and we lost him, so we searched for him in the valleys and the ravines. We said: "He has been carried off [[In al-Taj: istatara fulan: he was startled.]] or he has been seized." He said: So we spent the worst night any people ever spent. When he rose in the morning, behold, he came from the direction of Hira. We said: "O Messenger of Allah! We lost you and sought you, but did not find you, so we spent the worst night any people ever spent." He said: "The caller of the jinn came to me, so I went with him and recited the Qur'an to them." Then he set out with us and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. They asked him for provision, and they were from the jinn of the Jazira. He said: "For you is every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, which falls into your hands, as meaty as it can be, and every dung is fodder for your animals." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not cleanse yourselves with them, for they are the food of your jinn brothers."'" Ibn al-'Arabi said: Ibn Mas'ud is more knowledgeable than Ibn Abbas, because he witnessed it, whereas Ibn Abbas heard of it, and report is not like direct observation.

It has also been said that the jinn came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on two occasions: one in Mecca, which is the one Ibn Mas'ud mentioned, and the second at Nakhla, which is the one Ibn Abbas mentioned. Al-Bayhaqi said: What Abdullah ibn Abbas related is only about the first time the jinn heard the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ) and knew of his condition. At that time he did not recite to them, nor did he see them, as he related. Then the caller of the jinn came to him once more, and he went with him and recited the Qur'an to them, as Abdullah ibn Mas'ud related. Al-Bayhaqi said: The sound hadiths indicate that Ibn Mas'ud was not with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn, but he travelled with him when he set out with him and others, showing them the traces of the jinn and the traces of their fires. He said: It has been related through more than one chain that he was with him that night. This meaning has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf, and praise be to Allah.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an to the jinn. Who will go with me?" They remained silent. Then he said it a second time, then a third time. Then Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "I will go with you, O Messenger of Allah." So he set out until he came to al-Hajun, near the ravine of Abu Dubb [[The ravine of Abu Dubb is said to contain the burial place of Amina bint Wahb, the mother of the Prophet (ﷺ).]]. He drew a line for me and said: "Do not cross it." Then he went on to al-Hajun, and there descended upon him like men of the Hijaz [[Yuhdurun al-hijara, with the dal vowelled with damma or kasra: they lower the stones from a height to a low place.]] lowering stones with their feet, walking, striking their tambourines as women strike their tambourines, until they covered him, so I could not see him. I stood up, and he gestured to me with his hand to sit down. He recited the Qur'an, and his voice kept rising, and they pressed to the ground until I could no longer see them. When he turned back to me, he said: "Did you want to come to me?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "That was not for you. These are the jinn who came to listen to the Qur'an, then they turned back to their people as warners. They asked me for provision, so I provided them with bones and dung. Let none of you cleanse himself with a bone or with dung."

Ikrimah said: "They were twelve thousand from the island of Mosul." And in another narration: "He (ﷺ) set out with me until, when we came to the mosque that is by the wall of ʿAwf, he drew a line for me. Some of them came to him, and our companions said: 'They look like the Zutt [[al-Zutt: a people of India whose complexion tends toward black.]] and their faces like the makakiyy [[al-Makakiyy: plural of mikuk, a cup that is narrow at the top and wide in the middle, and a well-known measure among the people of Iraq with this same shape. Perhaps it is from the Arabs' saying: "His head was struck with a mikuk," by way of simile.]].' They said: 'What are you?' He said: 'I am the Prophet of Allah.' They said: 'Who will testify for you of that?' He said: 'This tree.' Then he said: 'O tree!' and it came dragging its roots, making a rustling sound, until it stood before him. He said: '[About] what do you testify?' It said: 'I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah.' Then it returned as it had come, dragging its roots over the stones, making a rustling sound, until it went back to how it had been. Then it is narrated that when he (ﷺ) had finished, he placed his head on the lap of Ibn Masʿud and slept, then woke up and said: '[Is there] any water for ablution?' He said: 'No, except that I have a flask with nabidh in it.' He said: '[Is it] not just dates and water?' So he performed ablution with it."

Third issue: The discussion of water has already passed in surah al-Hijr [[See vol. 10, p. 15 onward.]], and what may be used for istinja (cleansing after relieving oneself) in surah Bara'ah [[See vol. 8, p. 259 onward.]], so there is no point in repeating it.

Fourth issue: The scholars differed concerning the origin of the jinn. Isma'il narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that the jinn are the offspring of Iblis and mankind are the offspring of Adam, and among both there are believers and disbelievers, and they are partners in reward and punishment. Whoever among both is a believer is a friend of Allah, and whoever among both is a disbeliever is a devil. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that the jinn are the offspring of the jann and are not devils, and they believe, and among them there is the believer and the disbeliever; the devils are the offspring of Iblis, who do not die except together with Iblis.

They also differed concerning the entry of believing jinn into Paradise, according to their difference regarding their origin. Whoever claims that they are of the jann and not of the offspring of Iblis says: they enter Paradise by their faith. Whoever says that they are of the offspring of Iblis has two opinions: the first, which is the view of al-Hasan, is that they enter it; the second, which is the narration of Mujahid, is that they do not enter it, even if they are turned away from the Fire. This is related by al-Mawardi. It has already passed in surah al-Rahman [[See vol. 17, p. 181.]], at His saying: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 56], an explanation that they enter it.

Fifth issue: Al-Bayhaqi said in his narration: "They asked him for provision, and they were jinn of the island, and he said: '[For you is every bone].'" This is evidence that they eat and are fed. A group of disbelieving physicians and philosophers denied the jinn and said: they are simple substances, and their food is not valid, a presumption against Allah and a fabrication. The Qur'an and the Sunnah refute them. There is nothing among created beings that is simple, composite, or paired; rather, the One, the One [[al-Wahid al-Wahid: thus in some copies, and in some without repetition. In al-Shawkani: "Innama al-Wahid Allah subhanahu" (only the One is Allah, glory be to Him).]] is Allah, glory be to Him, and everything else is composite and is not one, however its state changes. It is not impossible that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them in their forms, just as he saw the angels. Most of the time they appear to us in the forms of snakes. In the Muwatta': a man newly married asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at midday to return to his family... the hadith, and in it: suddenly there was a huge snake coiled on the bed, so he thrust a spear at it and pinned it. And he mentioned the hadith. In the Sahih, he (ﷺ) said: "Indeed these houses have inhabitants, so if you see any of them, warn it three times; if it leaves, well and good, otherwise kill it, for it is a disbeliever." And he said: "Go and bury your companion." [[This should come before the preceding hadith, as in Ibn al-ʿArabi.]] This meaning has already passed in surah al-Baqarah [[See vol. 1, p. 315]], and the explanation of warning them. Some people held that this is specific to Medina, based on his saying in the Sahih: "Indeed in Medina there are jinn who have embraced Islam." This is a phrase specific to it, so the ruling is specific to it. We say: this indicates that other houses are similar to it, because he did not give as the cause the sanctity of Medina; rather the cause given was Islam, and that is general to other places. Do you not see his saying in the hadith, reporting about the jinn he met: "They were jinn of the island," and this is clear; it is supported by his saying: "And he forbade the inhabitants of the houses," and this is general. The discussion of this has already passed in surah al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: Indeed we have heard a wondrous Qur'an﴾. That is, wondrous in the eloquence of its speech. It was said: wondrous in the power of its admonitions. It was said: wondrous in its great blessing. It was said: a mighty Qur'an, of which there is no like. It was said: they mean great.

﴿It guides to righteousness﴾, that is, to the paths of right conduct. It was said: to the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He. And ﴿guides﴾ is in the position of an adjective, meaning "a guide." ﴿So we believed in it﴾, that is, we were guided by it and affirmed that it is from Allah. ﴿And we will never associate anyone with our Lord﴾.

That is, we will not return to Iblis nor obey him, for he was the one who had sent them to bring him news; then the jinn were pelted with shooting stars. It was also said: we will not take another god alongside Allah, for He alone has lordship. In this there is an amazement for the believers at the departure of the idolaters of Quraysh from what the jinn had grasped through contemplating the Qur'an.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A group of the jinn listened﴾, that is, they listened to the Prophet (ﷺ), and they knew that what he recited was the speech of Allah. The one listened to is not mentioned because the context indicates it. And "nafar" means a company; al-Khalil said: from three to ten.

Ibn Mas'ud... Isa al-Thaqafi read ﴿yahdi ila al-rushd﴾ with fath on the ra' and the shin.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾. ʿAlqamah, Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Ibn ʿAmir, Khalaf, Hafs and al-Sulami read "anna" with fath in the whole surah, in twelve places, and that is: ﴿that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾, ﴿and that He used to say﴾, ﴿and that we supposed﴾, ﴿and that there were men﴾, ﴿and that they supposed﴾, ﴿and that we touched the heaven﴾, ﴿and that we used to sit﴾, ﴿and that we do not know﴾, ﴿and that among us are the righteous﴾, ﴿and that we supposed that we would never escape Allah in the earth﴾, ﴿and that when we heard the guidance﴾, ﴿and that among us are the Muslims﴾, in coordination with His saying: "that he listened [a group]." And "anna he listened" allows only fath, because it is in the position of an active participle, "uhiya," so what follows it is conjoined to it. It was also said: it is governed by the pronoun in "fa-amanna bihi," meaning "and [we believed] in" that He, exalted is He, is the majesty of our Lord; and this is permissible though the pronoun is a genitive, because of the frequency of the preposition with "anna." It was also said: the meaning is "and we affirmed that He is the majesty of our Lord."

The rest read all of them with kasra, which is the correct reading, and Abu ʿUbayda and Abu Hatim preferred it, as coordinated with His saying: ﴿Indeed we have heard﴾, because all of it is the speech of the jinn. As for Abu Jaʿfar and Shaybah, they read with fath three places, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾, ﴿and that He used to say﴾, ﴿and that there were men﴾; they said: because it is from the revelation; and they read the rest with kasra, because it is from the speech of the jinn. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that when the servant of Allah stood up﴾ [al-Jinn: 19], all of them read with fath except Nafi', Shaybah, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal from ʿAsim, who read only with kasra. There is no disagreement about the fath of the hamza in ﴿that a group of the jinn listened﴾, ﴿that if they had remained upright﴾, ﴿and that the mosques are for Allah﴾, and ﴿that they had conveyed﴾. Likewise there is no disagreement about kasra after "qawl" (saying), such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: Indeed we have heard﴾ and ﴿Say: Indeed I only call upon my Lord﴾ [al-Jinn: 20], ﴿Say: I do not know﴾ [al-Jinn: 25], ﴿Say: Indeed I do not possess﴾ [al-Jinn: 21]. Likewise there is no disagreement about kasra after the fa' of the conditional, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed for him is the fire of Hell﴾ [al-Jinn: 23] and ﴿for indeed he sends forth before him﴾ [al-Jinn: 27], because it is a place of beginning.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾. "Jadd" in the language means greatness and majesty, and from it is the saying of Anas: "When a man had memorized al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, he became jadd in our eyes," that is, he became great and majestic. So the meaning of "jadd rabbina" is His greatness and majesty, as said by Ikrimah, Mujahid and Qatadah. It is also narrated from Mujahid: His remembrance. Anas ibn Malik, al-Hasan and Ikrimah also said: His wealth (ghina). From this comes the saying that fortune is "jadd," and a fortunate man is "majdud," that is, favored by fortune. In the hadith: "And no wealth of yours benefits the possessor of wealth (dhal-jadd)." Abu ʿUbayda and al-Khalil said: that is, the possessor of wealth, wealth from you; only obedience benefits him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: His power. Al-Dahhak: His act. Al-Qurazi and al-Dahhak also said: His bounties and blessings upon His creation. Abu ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash said: His dominion and authority. Al-Suddi said: His command. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord" means: exalted is our Lord. It was also said: they meant by it the "jadd" who is the father of the father (grandfather), and this would be part of the jinn's speech. Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, his son Jaʿfar al-Sadiq, and al-Rabiʿ said: Allah, exalted is He, has no "jadd"; the jinn said it out of ignorance, so they were not held accountable for it. Al-Qushayri said: It is permissible to apply the word "jadd" to Allah, exalted is He, for if it were not permissible it would not have been mentioned in the Qur'an; however, it is a word that gives a misleading impression, so avoiding it is better. The reading of Ikrimah is "jidd" with kasra on the jim, meaning the opposite of jest. Likewise Abu Hayawah and Muhammad ibn al-Sumaiqa read it. It is also narrated from Ibn al-Sumaiqa and Abu al-Ashhab "jadan rabbina," which means bounty and benefit. Ikrimah also read "jadd" with tanwin and "rabbuna" with damma, parsing it as the subject of "ta'ala," and "jaddan" as an accusative of specification. From Ikrimah also "jaddun" with tanwin and damma, "rabbuna" with damma, on the assumption: "exalted is the majesty of the majesty of our Lord," so the second "jadd" is a substitute for the first, and the genitive noun was dropped and the noun it governed was put in its place.

The meaning of the verse: "And that He, exalted is He, is the majesty of our Lord," that He should take a consort or a son for companionship and need of them; the Lord is exalted above rivals and peers.

They said to their people: "When the servant of Allah stood calling upon Him, they nearly became a mass upon him." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan and sahih. In this hadith there is evidence that he (ﷺ) did not see the jinn, but they attended him and heard his recitation. In it there is also evidence that the jinn were with the devils when they spied on the news, because of the devils, when they were struck by the shooting stars. And those struck by the shooting stars were also among the jinn. They were called devils, as He said: ﴿the devils of mankind and the jinn﴾ [al-An'am 6:112], for every rebellious one who departs from the obedience of Allah is a shaytan.

In al-Tirmidhi from Ibn Abbas, who said: The jinn used to ascend to the heaven to listen to the revelation. When they heard a word, they added nine to it. As for the word, it would be true, and as for what they added to it, it would be false. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, they were prevented from their seats. They mentioned that to Iblis, and shooting stars had not been thrown before that. Iblis said to them: "This matter is nothing but something that has happened on earth!" So he sent his soldiers, and they found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing praying between two mountains — I think he said in Mecca — so they came to him and informed him. He said: "This is the event that has happened on the earth." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan and sahih. This hadith indicates that the jinn were struck as the devils were struck.

In the narration of al-Suddi: When they were struck, they came to Iblis and informed him of what had happened to them. He said: "Bring me from every land a handful of dust that I may smell it." They brought it to him, and he smelled it and said: "Your companion is in Mecca." So he sent a company of the jinn — it is said they were seven, and it is said nine, among them Zawba'a. Zirr narrated from Asim: The company of Zawba'a and his companions came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Thumali said: They were from the Banu al-Shaysaban, who are the most numerous of the jinn and the strongest in power, and they are the general body of Iblis's soldiers. Asim also narrated from Zirr: They were seven men, three from the people of Harran and four from the people of Nasibin. Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: They were nine from the people of Nasibin (a village in Yemen, other than the one in Iraq) [[We did not find the Nasibin mentioned by the author in Mu'jam maAsta'jam by al-Bakri, nor in Mu'jam al-Buldan by Yaqut, nor in what the author of Taj al-'Arus quoted from Yaqut.]]. It was said: The jinn who came to Mecca were the jinn of Nasibin, and those who came to him at Nakhla were the jinn of Nineveh. The explanation of this has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf [[See vol. 16, p. 211.]]. Ikrima said: The surah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite was "Read in the name of your Lord" [al-'Alaq 96:1]. The explanation of the names of the company of the jinn has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf, so there is no point in repeating it.

It is said that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw the jinn on the night of the jinn, and this is more firmly established. Amir al-Sha'bi narrated: I asked Alqama, "Was Ibn Mas'ud present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?" Alqama said: "I asked Ibn Mas'ud, 'Was any of you present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?' He said: 'No, but we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night, and we lost him, so we searched for him in the valleys and the ravines. We said: "He has been carried off [[In al-Taj: istatara fulan: he was startled.]] or he has been seized." He said: So we spent the worst night any people ever spent. When he rose in the morning, behold, he came from the direction of Hira. We said: "O Messenger of Allah! We lost you and sought you, but did not find you, so we spent the worst night any people ever spent." He said: "The caller of the jinn came to me, so I went with him and recited the Qur'an to them." Then he set out with us and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. They asked him for provision, and they were from the jinn of the Jazira. He said: "For you is every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, which falls into your hands, as meaty as it can be, and every dung is fodder for your animals." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not cleanse yourselves with them, for they are the food of your jinn brothers."'" Ibn al-'Arabi said: Ibn Mas'ud is more knowledgeable than Ibn Abbas, because he witnessed it, whereas Ibn Abbas heard of it, and report is not like direct observation.

It has also been said that the jinn came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on two occasions: one in Mecca, which is the one Ibn Mas'ud mentioned, and the second at Nakhla, which is the one Ibn Abbas mentioned. Al-Bayhaqi said: What Abdullah ibn Abbas related is only about the first time the jinn heard the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ) and knew of his condition. At that time he did not recite to them, nor did he see them, as he related. Then the caller of the jinn came to him once more, and he went with him and recited the Qur'an to them, as Abdullah ibn Mas'ud related. Al-Bayhaqi said: The sound hadiths indicate that Ibn Mas'ud was not with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn, but he travelled with him when he set out with him and others, showing them the traces of the jinn and the traces of their fires. He said: It has been related through more than one chain that he was with him that night. This meaning has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf, and praise be to Allah.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an to the jinn. Who will go with me?" They remained silent. Then he said it a second time, then a third time. Then Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "I will go with you, O Messenger of Allah." So he set out until he came to al-Hajun, near the ravine of Abu Dubb [[The ravine of Abu Dubb is said to contain the burial place of Amina bint Wahb, the mother of the Prophet (ﷺ).]]. He drew a line for me and said: "Do not cross it." Then he went on to al-Hajun, and there descended upon him like men of the Hijaz [[Yuhdurun al-hijara, with the dal vowelled with damma or kasra: they lower the stones from a height to a low place.]] lowering stones with their feet, walking, striking their tambourines as women strike their tambourines, until they covered him, so I could not see him. I stood up, and he gestured to me with his hand to sit down. He recited the Qur'an, and his voice kept rising, and they pressed to the ground until I could no longer see them. When he turned back to me, he said: "Did you want to come to me?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "That was not for you. These are the jinn who came to listen to the Qur'an, then they turned back to their people as warners. They asked me for provision, so I provided them with bones and dung. Let none of you cleanse himself with a bone or with dung."

Ikrimah said: "They were twelve thousand from the island of Mosul." And in another narration: "He (ﷺ) set out with me until, when we came to the mosque that is by the wall of ʿAwf, he drew a line for me. Some of them came to him, and our companions said: 'They look like the Zutt [[al-Zutt: a people of India whose complexion tends toward black.]] and their faces like the makakiyy [[al-Makakiyy: plural of mikuk, a cup that is narrow at the top and wide in the middle, and a well-known measure among the people of Iraq with this same shape. Perhaps it is from the Arabs' saying: "His head was struck with a mikuk," by way of simile.]].' They said: 'What are you?' He said: 'I am the Prophet of Allah.' They said: 'Who will testify for you of that?' He said: 'This tree.' Then he said: 'O tree!' and it came dragging its roots, making a rustling sound, until it stood before him. He said: '[About] what do you testify?' It said: 'I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah.' Then it returned as it had come, dragging its roots over the stones, making a rustling sound, until it went back to how it had been. Then it is narrated that when he (ﷺ) had finished, he placed his head on the lap of Ibn Masʿud and slept, then woke up and said: '[Is there] any water for ablution?' He said: 'No, except that I have a flask with nabidh in it.' He said: '[Is it] not just dates and water?' So he performed ablution with it."

Third issue: The discussion of water has already passed in surah al-Hijr [[See vol. 10, p. 15 onward.]], and what may be used for istinja (cleansing after relieving oneself) in surah Bara'ah [[See vol. 8, p. 259 onward.]], so there is no point in repeating it.

Fourth issue: The scholars differed concerning the origin of the jinn. Isma'il narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that the jinn are the offspring of Iblis and mankind are the offspring of Adam, and among both there are believers and disbelievers, and they are partners in reward and punishment. Whoever among both is a believer is a friend of Allah, and whoever among both is a disbeliever is a devil. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that the jinn are the offspring of the jann and are not devils, and they believe, and among them there is the believer and the disbeliever; the devils are the offspring of Iblis, who do not die except together with Iblis.

They also differed concerning the entry of believing jinn into Paradise, according to their difference regarding their origin. Whoever claims that they are of the jann and not of the offspring of Iblis says: they enter Paradise by their faith. Whoever says that they are of the offspring of Iblis has two opinions: the first, which is the view of al-Hasan, is that they enter it; the second, which is the narration of Mujahid, is that they do not enter it, even if they are turned away from the Fire. This is related by al-Mawardi. It has already passed in surah al-Rahman [[See vol. 17, p. 181.]], at His saying: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 56], an explanation that they enter it.

Fifth issue: Al-Bayhaqi said in his narration: "They asked him for provision, and they were jinn of the island, and he said: '[For you is every bone].'" This is evidence that they eat and are fed. A group of disbelieving physicians and philosophers denied the jinn and said: they are simple substances, and their food is not valid, a presumption against Allah and a fabrication. The Qur'an and the Sunnah refute them. There is nothing among created beings that is simple, composite, or paired; rather, the One, the One [[al-Wahid al-Wahid: thus in some copies, and in some without repetition. In al-Shawkani: "Innama al-Wahid Allah subhanahu" (only the One is Allah, glory be to Him).]] is Allah, glory be to Him, and everything else is composite and is not one, however its state changes. It is not impossible that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them in their forms, just as he saw the angels. Most of the time they appear to us in the forms of snakes. In the Muwatta': a man newly married asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at midday to return to his family... the hadith, and in it: suddenly there was a huge snake coiled on the bed, so he thrust a spear at it and pinned it. And he mentioned the hadith. In the Sahih, he (ﷺ) said: "Indeed these houses have inhabitants, so if you see any of them, warn it three times; if it leaves, well and good, otherwise kill it, for it is a disbeliever." And he said: "Go and bury your companion." [[This should come before the preceding hadith, as in Ibn al-ʿArabi.]] This meaning has already passed in surah al-Baqarah [[See vol. 1, p. 315]], and the explanation of warning them. Some people held that this is specific to Medina, based on his saying in the Sahih: "Indeed in Medina there are jinn who have embraced Islam." This is a phrase specific to it, so the ruling is specific to it. We say: this indicates that other houses are similar to it, because he did not give as the cause the sanctity of Medina; rather the cause given was Islam, and that is general to other places. Do you not see his saying in the hadith, reporting about the jinn he met: "They were jinn of the island," and this is clear; it is supported by his saying: "And he forbade the inhabitants of the houses," and this is general. The discussion of this has already passed in surah al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: Indeed we have heard a wondrous Qur'an﴾. That is, wondrous in the eloquence of its speech. It was said: wondrous in the power of its admonitions. It was said: wondrous in its great blessing. It was said: a mighty Qur'an, of which there is no like. It was said: they mean great.

﴿It guides to righteousness﴾, that is, to the paths of right conduct. It was said: to the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He. And ﴿guides﴾ is in the position of an adjective, meaning "a guide." ﴿So we believed in it﴾, that is, we were guided by it and affirmed that it is from Allah. ﴿And we will never associate anyone with our Lord﴾.

That is, we will not return to Iblis nor obey him, for he was the one who had sent them to bring him news; then the jinn were pelted with shooting stars. It was also said: we will not take another god alongside Allah, for He alone has lordship. In this there is an amazement for the believers at the departure of the idolaters of Quraysh from what the jinn had grasped through contemplating the Qur'an.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A group of the jinn listened﴾, that is, they listened to the Prophet (ﷺ), and they knew that what he recited was the speech of Allah. The one listened to is not mentioned because the context indicates it. And "nafar" means a company; al-Khalil said: from three to ten.

Ibn Mas'ud... Isa al-Thaqafi read ﴿yahdi ila al-rushd﴾ with fath on the ra' and the shin.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾. ʿAlqamah, Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Ibn ʿAmir, Khalaf, Hafs and al-Sulami read "anna" with fath in the whole surah, in twelve places, and that is: ﴿that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾, ﴿and that He used to say﴾, ﴿and that we supposed﴾, ﴿and that there were men﴾, ﴿and that they supposed﴾, ﴿and that we touched the heaven﴾, ﴿and that we used to sit﴾, ﴿and that we do not know﴾, ﴿and that among us are the righteous﴾, ﴿and that we supposed that we would never escape Allah in the earth﴾, ﴿and that when we heard the guidance﴾, ﴿and that among us are the Muslims﴾, in coordination with His saying: "that he listened [a group]." And "anna he listened" allows only fath, because it is in the position of an active participle, "uhiya," so what follows it is conjoined to it. It was also said: it is governed by the pronoun in "fa-amanna bihi," meaning "and [we believed] in" that He, exalted is He, is the majesty of our Lord; and this is permissible though the pronoun is a genitive, because of the frequency of the preposition with "anna." It was also said: the meaning is "and we affirmed that He is the majesty of our Lord."

The rest read all of them with kasra, which is the correct reading, and Abu ʿUbayda and Abu Hatim preferred it, as coordinated with His saying: ﴿Indeed we have heard﴾, because all of it is the speech of the jinn. As for Abu Jaʿfar and Shaybah, they read with fath three places, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾, ﴿and that He used to say﴾, ﴿and that there were men﴾; they said: because it is from the revelation; and they read the rest with kasra, because it is from the speech of the jinn. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that when the servant of Allah stood up﴾ [al-Jinn: 19], all of them read with fath except Nafi', Shaybah, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal from ʿAsim, who read only with kasra. There is no disagreement about the fath of the hamza in ﴿that a group of the jinn listened﴾, ﴿that if they had remained upright﴾, ﴿and that the mosques are for Allah﴾, and ﴿that they had conveyed﴾. Likewise there is no disagreement about kasra after "qawl" (saying), such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: Indeed we have heard﴾ and ﴿Say: Indeed I only call upon my Lord﴾ [al-Jinn: 20], ﴿Say: I do not know﴾ [al-Jinn: 25], ﴿Say: Indeed I do not possess﴾ [al-Jinn: 21]. Likewise there is no disagreement about kasra after the fa' of the conditional, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed for him is the fire of Hell﴾ [al-Jinn: 23] and ﴿for indeed he sends forth before him﴾ [al-Jinn: 27], because it is a place of beginning.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾. "Jadd" in the language means greatness and majesty, and from it is the saying of Anas: "When a man had memorized al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, he became jadd in our eyes," that is, he became great and majestic. So the meaning of "jadd rabbina" is His greatness and majesty, as said by Ikrimah, Mujahid and Qatadah. It is also narrated from Mujahid: His remembrance. Anas ibn Malik, al-Hasan and Ikrimah also said: His wealth (ghina). From this comes the saying that fortune is "jadd," and a fortunate man is "majdud," that is, favored by fortune. In the hadith: "And no wealth of yours benefits the possessor of wealth (dhal-jadd)." Abu ʿUbayda and al-Khalil said: that is, the possessor of wealth, wealth from you; only obedience benefits him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: His power. Al-Dahhak: His act. Al-Qurazi and al-Dahhak also said: His bounties and blessings upon His creation. Abu ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash said: His dominion and authority. Al-Suddi said: His command. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord" means: exalted is our Lord. It was also said: they meant by it the "jadd" who is the father of the father (grandfather), and this would be part of the jinn's speech. Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, his son Jaʿfar al-Sadiq, and al-Rabiʿ said: Allah, exalted is He, has no "jadd"; the jinn said it out of ignorance, so they were not held accountable for it. Al-Qushayri said: It is permissible to apply the word "jadd" to Allah, exalted is He, for if it were not permissible it would not have been mentioned in the Qur'an; however, it is a word that gives a misleading impression, so avoiding it is better. The reading of Ikrimah is "jidd" with kasra on the jim, meaning the opposite of jest. Likewise Abu Hayawah and Muhammad ibn al-Sumaiqa read it. It is also narrated from Ibn al-Sumaiqa and Abu al-Ashhab "jadan rabbina," which means bounty and benefit. Ikrimah also read "jadd" with tanwin and "rabbuna" with damma, parsing it as the subject of "ta'ala," and "jaddan" as an accusative of specification. From Ikrimah also "jaddun" with tanwin and damma, "rabbuna" with damma, on the assumption: "exalted is the majesty of the majesty of our Lord," so the second "jadd" is a substitute for the first, and the genitive noun was dropped and the noun it governed was put in its place.

The meaning of the verse: "And that He, exalted is He, is the majesty of our Lord," that He should take a consort or a son for companionship and need of them; the Lord is exalted above rivals and peers.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 72, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Surat al-Jinn is Meccan, according to the consensus. It has twenty-eight verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened, and they said: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord. And exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has taken neither a consort nor a son."﴾

There are five issues in this.

The first: His saying, the Exalted: "Say: It has been revealed to me." That is, say, O Muhammad, to your community: Allah revealed to me through Jibril that a company of the jinn listened to me. He (ﷺ) did not know about it before it was revealed to him. This is what Ibn Abbas and others said, as will come. Ibn Abi Ablah read "uhiya" [[In the originals it is written (wahiya), and the correct reading is what we have established, which agrees with what appears in (Taj al-'Arus: wahy). It says: Juwaybir al-Asadi recited: (Qul uhiya ilayya), and it did not attribute the reading to Ibn Abi Ablah.]] according to the original form. It is said: awha ilayhi and wahaa, so the waw was changed into a hamza. From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered at their appointed time﴾ [al-Mursalat 77:11], and it is metathesis (qalb, the transposition of letters), whose permissibility is absolute in every waw that carries a damma. Al-Mazini also applied it absolutely to the waw with a kasra, as in ishah (for wishah, a sash), isadah (for wisadah, a support), and "i'a akhihi" (for wi'a akhihi, the "container of his brother") and similar forms.

The second: It has been disputed whether the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them or not. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that he did not see them, because of His saying "listened" and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when We turned to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:29]. In the Sahih of Muslim and al-Tirmidhi [[The wording is Muslim's; as for al-Tirmidhi, his wording contains an addition.]] from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recite to the jinn nor see them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with a group of his companions, intending Souq Ukaz, and the devils had been prevented from the news of the heaven, and shooting stars were sent against them. The devils returned to their people, and they said: "What is the matter with you?" They said: "We have been prevented from the news of the heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us!" They said: "Nothing but something new has happened. Strike the eastern and western parts of the earth and see what this is that has come between us and the news of the heaven." So they set off striking the eastern and western parts of the earth. The company that took the way toward Tihama, and he was at Nakhla [[So it is in (a), (h), (t), and it is the correct reading.]], intending Souq Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: "This is what has come between us and the news of the heaven." They returned to their people and said: "O our people, indeed we have heard a Qur'an that is wondrous [[In (h): "Indeed we have heard a book sent down after Musa, a Qur'an that is wondrous ..." etc.]], which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened﴾.

He related it from Ibn Abbas, who said: The saying of the jinn to their people, when "the servant of Allah stood calling upon Him, they nearly became a mass upon him" [al-Jinn 72:19], He said: When they saw him praying and his companions praying with his prayer, prostrating with his prostration. He said [[In (h): "and prostrating with him ..."]]: They marvelled at the obedience of his companions to him. They said to their people: "When the servant of Allah stood calling upon Him, they nearly became a mass upon him." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan and sahih. In this hadith there is evidence that he (ﷺ) did not see the jinn, but they attended him and heard his recitation. In it there is also evidence that the jinn were with the devils when they spied on the news, because of the devils, when they were struck by the shooting stars. And those struck by the shooting stars were also among the jinn. They were called devils, as He said: ﴿the devils of mankind and the jinn﴾ [al-An'am 6:112], for every rebellious one who departs from the obedience of Allah is a shaytan.

In al-Tirmidhi from Ibn Abbas, who said: The jinn used to ascend to the heaven to listen to the revelation. When they heard a word, they added nine to it. As for the word, it would be true, and as for what they added to it, it would be false. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, they were prevented from their seats. They mentioned that to Iblis, and shooting stars had not been thrown before that. Iblis said to them: "This matter is nothing but something that has happened on earth!" So he sent his soldiers, and they found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing praying between two mountains — I think he said in Mecca — so they came to him and informed him. He said: "This is the event that has happened on the earth." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan and sahih. This hadith indicates that the jinn were struck as the devils were struck.

In the narration of al-Suddi: When they were struck, they came to Iblis and informed him of what had happened to them. He said: "Bring me from every land a handful of dust that I may smell it." They brought it to him, and he smelled it and said: "Your companion is in Mecca." So he sent a company of the jinn — it is said they were seven, and it is said nine, among them Zawba'a. Zirr narrated from Asim: The company of Zawba'a and his companions came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Thumali said: They were from the Banu al-Shaysaban, who are the most numerous of the jinn and the strongest in power, and they are the general body of Iblis's soldiers. Asim also narrated from Zirr: They were seven men, three from the people of Harran and four from the people of Nasibin. Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: They were nine from the people of Nasibin (a village in Yemen, other than the one in Iraq) [[We did not find the Nasibin mentioned by the author in Mu'jam maAsta'jam by al-Bakri, nor in Mu'jam al-Buldan by Yaqut, nor in what the author of Taj al-'Arus quoted from Yaqut.]]. It was said: The jinn who came to Mecca were the jinn of Nasibin, and those who came to him at Nakhla were the jinn of Nineveh. The explanation of this has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf [[See vol. 16, p. 211.]]. Ikrima said: The surah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite was "Read in the name of your Lord" [al-'Alaq 96:1]. The explanation of the names of the company of the jinn has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf, so there is no point in repeating it.

It is said that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw the jinn on the night of the jinn, and this is more firmly established. Amir al-Sha'bi narrated: I asked Alqama, "Was Ibn Mas'ud present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?" Alqama said: "I asked Ibn Mas'ud, 'Was any of you present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?' He said: 'No, but we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night, and we lost him, so we searched for him in the valleys and the ravines. We said: "He has been carried off [[In al-Taj: istatara fulan: he was startled.]] or he has been seized." He said: So we spent the worst night any people ever spent. When he rose in the morning, behold, he came from the direction of Hira. We said: "O Messenger of Allah! We lost you and sought you, but did not find you, so we spent the worst night any people ever spent." He said: "The caller of the jinn came to me, so I went with him and recited the Qur'an to them." Then he set out with us and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. They asked him for provision, and they were from the jinn of the Jazira. He said: "For you is every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, which falls into your hands, as meaty as it can be, and every dung is fodder for your animals." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not cleanse yourselves with them, for they are the food of your jinn brothers."'" Ibn al-'Arabi said: Ibn Mas'ud is more knowledgeable than Ibn Abbas, because he witnessed it, whereas Ibn Abbas heard of it, and report is not like direct observation.

It has also been said that the jinn came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on two occasions: one in Mecca, which is the one Ibn Mas'ud mentioned, and the second at Nakhla, which is the one Ibn Abbas mentioned. Al-Bayhaqi said: What Abdullah ibn Abbas related is only about the first time the jinn heard the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ) and knew of his condition. At that time he did not recite to them, nor did he see them, as he related. Then the caller of the jinn came to him once more, and he went with him and recited the Qur'an to them, as Abdullah ibn Mas'ud related. Al-Bayhaqi said: The sound hadiths indicate that Ibn Mas'ud was not with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn, but he travelled with him when he set out with him and others, showing them the traces of the jinn and the traces of their fires. He said: It has been related through more than one chain that he was with him that night. This meaning has already passed in surat al-Ahqaf, and praise be to Allah.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an to the jinn. Who will go with me?" They remained silent. Then he said it a second time, then a third time. Then Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "I will go with you, O Messenger of Allah." So he set out until he came to al-Hajun, near the ravine of Abu Dubb [[The ravine of Abu Dubb is said to contain the burial place of Amina bint Wahb, the mother of the Prophet (ﷺ).]]. He drew a line for me and said: "Do not cross it." Then he went on to al-Hajun, and there descended upon him like men of the Hijaz [[Yuhdurun al-hijara, with the dal vowelled with damma or kasra: they lower the stones from a height to a low place.]] lowering stones with their feet, walking, striking their tambourines as women strike their tambourines, until they covered him, so I could not see him. I stood up, and he gestured to me with his hand to sit down. He recited the Qur'an, and his voice kept rising, and they pressed to the ground until I could no longer see them. When he turned back to me, he said: "Did you want to come to me?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "That was not for you. These are the jinn who came to listen to the Qur'an, then they turned back to their people as warners. They asked me for provision, so I provided them with bones and dung. Let none of you cleanse himself with a bone or with dung."

Ikrimah said: "They were twelve thousand from the island of Mosul." And in another narration: "He (ﷺ) set out with me until, when we came to the mosque that is by the wall of ʿAwf, he drew a line for me. Some of them came to him, and our companions said: 'They look like the Zutt [[al-Zutt: a people of India whose complexion tends toward black.]] and their faces like the makakiyy [[al-Makakiyy: plural of mikuk, a cup that is narrow at the top and wide in the middle, and a well-known measure among the people of Iraq with this same shape. Perhaps it is from the Arabs' saying: "His head was struck with a mikuk," by way of simile.]].' They said: 'What are you?' He said: 'I am the Prophet of Allah.' They said: 'Who will testify for you of that?' He said: 'This tree.' Then he said: 'O tree!' and it came dragging its roots, making a rustling sound, until it stood before him. He said: '[About] what do you testify?' It said: 'I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah.' Then it returned as it had come, dragging its roots over the stones, making a rustling sound, until it went back to how it had been. Then it is narrated that when he (ﷺ) had finished, he placed his head on the lap of Ibn Masʿud and slept, then woke up and said: '[Is there] any water for ablution?' He said: 'No, except that I have a flask with nabidh in it.' He said: '[Is it] not just dates and water?' So he performed ablution with it."

Third issue: The discussion of water has already passed in surah al-Hijr [[See vol. 10, p. 15 onward.]], and what may be used for istinja (cleansing after relieving oneself) in surah Bara'ah [[See vol. 8, p. 259 onward.]], so there is no point in repeating it.

Fourth issue: The scholars differed concerning the origin of the jinn. Isma'il narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that the jinn are the offspring of Iblis and mankind are the offspring of Adam, and among both there are believers and disbelievers, and they are partners in reward and punishment. Whoever among both is a believer is a friend of Allah, and whoever among both is a disbeliever is a devil. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that the jinn are the offspring of the jann and are not devils, and they believe, and among them there is the believer and the disbeliever; the devils are the offspring of Iblis, who do not die except together with Iblis.

They also differed concerning the entry of believing jinn into Paradise, according to their difference regarding their origin. Whoever claims that they are of the jann and not of the offspring of Iblis says: they enter Paradise by their faith. Whoever says that they are of the offspring of Iblis has two opinions: the first, which is the view of al-Hasan, is that they enter it; the second, which is the narration of Mujahid, is that they do not enter it, even if they are turned away from the Fire. This is related by al-Mawardi. It has already passed in surah al-Rahman [[See vol. 17, p. 181.]], at His saying: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 56], an explanation that they enter it.

Fifth issue: Al-Bayhaqi said in his narration: "They asked him for provision, and they were jinn of the island, and he said: '[For you is every bone].'" This is evidence that they eat and are fed. A group of disbelieving physicians and philosophers denied the jinn and said: they are simple substances, and their food is not valid, a presumption against Allah and a fabrication. The Qur'an and the Sunnah refute them. There is nothing among created beings that is simple, composite, or paired; rather, the One, the One [[al-Wahid al-Wahid: thus in some copies, and in some without repetition. In al-Shawkani: "Innama al-Wahid Allah subhanahu" (only the One is Allah, glory be to Him).]] is Allah, glory be to Him, and everything else is composite and is not one, however its state changes. It is not impossible that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them in their forms, just as he saw the angels. Most of the time they appear to us in the forms of snakes. In the Muwatta': a man newly married asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at midday to return to his family... the hadith, and in it: suddenly there was a huge snake coiled on the bed, so he thrust a spear at it and pinned it. And he mentioned the hadith. In the Sahih, he (ﷺ) said: "Indeed these houses have inhabitants, so if you see any of them, warn it three times; if it leaves, well and good, otherwise kill it, for it is a disbeliever." And he said: "Go and bury your companion." [[This should come before the preceding hadith, as in Ibn al-ʿArabi.]] This meaning has already passed in surah al-Baqarah [[See vol. 1, p. 315]], and the explanation of warning them. Some people held that this is specific to Medina, based on his saying in the Sahih: "Indeed in Medina there are jinn who have embraced Islam." This is a phrase specific to it, so the ruling is specific to it. We say: this indicates that other houses are similar to it, because he did not give as the cause the sanctity of Medina; rather the cause given was Islam, and that is general to other places. Do you not see his saying in the hadith, reporting about the jinn he met: "They were jinn of the island," and this is clear; it is supported by his saying: "And he forbade the inhabitants of the houses," and this is general. The discussion of this has already passed in surah al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: Indeed we have heard a wondrous Qur'an﴾. That is, wondrous in the eloquence of its speech. It was said: wondrous in the power of its admonitions. It was said: wondrous in its great blessing. It was said: a mighty Qur'an, of which there is no like. It was said: they mean great.

﴿It guides to righteousness﴾, that is, to the paths of right conduct. It was said: to the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He. And ﴿guides﴾ is in the position of an adjective, meaning "a guide." ﴿So we believed in it﴾, that is, we were guided by it and affirmed that it is from Allah. ﴿And we will never associate anyone with our Lord﴾.

That is, we will not return to Iblis nor obey him, for he was the one who had sent them to bring him news; then the jinn were pelted with shooting stars. It was also said: we will not take another god alongside Allah, for He alone has lordship. In this there is an amazement for the believers at the departure of the idolaters of Quraysh from what the jinn had grasped through contemplating the Qur'an.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A group of the jinn listened﴾, that is, they listened to the Prophet (ﷺ), and they knew that what he recited was the speech of Allah. The one listened to is not mentioned because the context indicates it. And "nafar" means a company; al-Khalil said: from three to ten.

Ibn Mas'ud... Isa al-Thaqafi read ﴿yahdi ila al-rushd﴾ with fath on the ra' and the shin.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾. ʿAlqamah, Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Ibn ʿAmir, Khalaf, Hafs and al-Sulami read "anna" with fath in the whole surah, in twelve places, and that is: ﴿that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾, ﴿and that He used to say﴾, ﴿and that we supposed﴾, ﴿and that there were men﴾, ﴿and that they supposed﴾, ﴿and that we touched the heaven﴾, ﴿and that we used to sit﴾, ﴿and that we do not know﴾, ﴿and that among us are the righteous﴾, ﴿and that we supposed that we would never escape Allah in the earth﴾, ﴿and that when we heard the guidance﴾, ﴿and that among us are the Muslims﴾, in coordination with His saying: "that he listened [a group]." And "anna he listened" allows only fath, because it is in the position of an active participle, "uhiya," so what follows it is conjoined to it. It was also said: it is governed by the pronoun in "fa-amanna bihi," meaning "and [we believed] in" that He, exalted is He, is the majesty of our Lord; and this is permissible though the pronoun is a genitive, because of the frequency of the preposition with "anna." It was also said: the meaning is "and we affirmed that He is the majesty of our Lord."

The rest read all of them with kasra, which is the correct reading, and Abu ʿUbayda and Abu Hatim preferred it, as coordinated with His saying: ﴿Indeed we have heard﴾, because all of it is the speech of the jinn. As for Abu Jaʿfar and Shaybah, they read with fath three places, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾, ﴿and that He used to say﴾, ﴿and that there were men﴾; they said: because it is from the revelation; and they read the rest with kasra, because it is from the speech of the jinn. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that when the servant of Allah stood up﴾ [al-Jinn: 19], all of them read with fath except Nafi', Shaybah, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal from ʿAsim, who read only with kasra. There is no disagreement about the fath of the hamza in ﴿that a group of the jinn listened﴾, ﴿that if they had remained upright﴾, ﴿and that the mosques are for Allah﴾, and ﴿that they had conveyed﴾. Likewise there is no disagreement about kasra after "qawl" (saying), such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: Indeed we have heard﴾ and ﴿Say: Indeed I only call upon my Lord﴾ [al-Jinn: 20], ﴿Say: I do not know﴾ [al-Jinn: 25], ﴿Say: Indeed I do not possess﴾ [al-Jinn: 21]. Likewise there is no disagreement about kasra after the fa' of the conditional, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed for him is the fire of Hell﴾ [al-Jinn: 23] and ﴿for indeed he sends forth before him﴾ [al-Jinn: 27], because it is a place of beginning.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord﴾. "Jadd" in the language means greatness and majesty, and from it is the saying of Anas: "When a man had memorized al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, he became jadd in our eyes," that is, he became great and majestic. So the meaning of "jadd rabbina" is His greatness and majesty, as said by Ikrimah, Mujahid and Qatadah. It is also narrated from Mujahid: His remembrance. Anas ibn Malik, al-Hasan and Ikrimah also said: His wealth (ghina). From this comes the saying that fortune is "jadd," and a fortunate man is "majdud," that is, favored by fortune. In the hadith: "And no wealth of yours benefits the possessor of wealth (dhal-jadd)." Abu ʿUbayda and al-Khalil said: that is, the possessor of wealth, wealth from you; only obedience benefits him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: His power. Al-Dahhak: His act. Al-Qurazi and al-Dahhak also said: His bounties and blessings upon His creation. Abu ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash said: His dominion and authority. Al-Suddi said: His command. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord" means: exalted is our Lord. It was also said: they meant by it the "jadd" who is the father of the father (grandfather), and this would be part of the jinn's speech. Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, his son Jaʿfar al-Sadiq, and al-Rabiʿ said: Allah, exalted is He, has no "jadd"; the jinn said it out of ignorance, so they were not held accountable for it. Al-Qushayri said: It is permissible to apply the word "jadd" to Allah, exalted is He, for if it were not permissible it would not have been mentioned in the Qur'an; however, it is a word that gives a misleading impression, so avoiding it is better. The reading of Ikrimah is "jidd" with kasra on the jim, meaning the opposite of jest. Likewise Abu Hayawah and Muhammad ibn al-Sumaiqa read it. It is also narrated from Ibn al-Sumaiqa and Abu al-Ashhab "jadan rabbina," which means bounty and benefit. Ikrimah also read "jadd" with tanwin and "rabbuna" with damma, parsing it as the subject of "ta'ala," and "jaddan" as an accusative of specification. From Ikrimah also "jaddun" with tanwin and damma, "rabbuna" with damma, on the assumption: "exalted is the majesty of the majesty of our Lord," so the second "jadd" is a substitute for the first, and the genitive noun was dropped and the noun it governed was put in its place.

The meaning of the verse: "And that He, exalted is He, is the majesty of our Lord," that He should take a consort or a son for companionship and need of them; the Lord is exalted above rivals and peers.

The Words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And that it was that our foolish one would utter outrageous lies against Allah﴾. The pronoun in "annahu" (that it) refers to the matter or the statement (ḍamīr al-sha'n, the pronoun of the matter). Its noun is "kāna," and what follows is the predicate. It is also permissible for "kāna" to be redundant (zā'idah, meaning grammatically superfluous). The "foolish one" (safīh) here is Iblis, according to Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj and Qatadah. Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa narrated it from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ). It has also been said that the foolish one refers to the polytheists among the jinn. Qatadah said: "Their foolish one disobeyed (Allah) just as the foolish one among mankind disobeyed Him." Al-shaṭaṭ and al-ishtiṭāṭ mean excessiveness in disbelief. Abu Malik said: it is injustice (jawr). Al-Kalbi said: it is lying (kadhib). Its root meaning is distance, so it is used for injustice because of its distance from justice, and for lying because of its distance from truth. The poet said:

"In whatever state they judged you, they went to extremes, and that was nothing but where [their] aim struck you, the spear-thrust."

The Words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And that we had thought﴾, meaning we supposed that neither mankind nor the jinn would utter lies against Allah. Therefore we believed them in their claim that Allah has a consort and a son, until we heard the Qur'an and perceived the truth through it. Ya'qub, al-Jahdari and Ibn Abi Ishaq recited "an lan taqūla" (with the verb in its full form). [Al-Alusi said: "taqūlu" originally was "tataqawwalu" with two tā's, one of which was deleted. "Kadhiban" is a verbal noun emphasising the meaning, because lying is the same as "taqawwul" (fabricating speech).] It has also been said: the report of the jinn ends here, and Allah the Exalted then says: ﴿And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn﴾. Whoever reads "anna" with a fatḥah (opening vowel) and makes it part of the speech of the jinn, links it back to His words: "that it was [revealed to me] that a group of the jinn listened" (al-Jinn 1). Whoever reads it with a kasrah (ʾinna) makes it a new sentence beginning from the words of Allah the Exalted.

What is meant is the practice they used to follow: a man, when he camped in a valley, would say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the evil of the foolish ones of his people," and he would spend the night under his protection until morning. This was said by al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd and others. Muqatil said: the first people who sought refuge with the jinn were a group from the people of Yemen, then the Banu Hanifah, then this spread among the Arabs. When Islam came, they sought refuge in Allah and abandoned them.

Kardam ibn Abi al-Sa'ib said: "I went out with my father to Medina at the time when the Prophet (ﷺ) was first mentioned. Night overtook us at the abode of a shepherd. When half the night had passed, a wolf came and seized a lamb from the flock. The shepherd said: 'O Amir of the valley, I am your neighbour!' A caller called out: 'O Sarhan, release it!' and the lamb came running (yashtadd, meaning dashing off)."

Allah the Exalted revealed to His Messenger in Mecca: ﴿And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in ruhaq﴾, meaning the jinn increased mankind in ruhaq, that is, in sin and wrongdoing. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah. Al-ruhaq in the speech of the Arabs means sin and the committing of what is forbidden. A man is called rahiq when he is such. From it is the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and humiliation will cover them﴾ (Yunus 27). The poet al-A'sha said:

"Nothing benefits me apart from seeing her; can a lover be healed unless he has been struck by ruhaq?"

He means sin. The increase is ascribed to the jinn because they were the cause of it. Mujahid also said: ﴿so they increased them﴾ means that mankind increased the jinn in transgression through this seeking of refuge, until the jinn said: "We have become masters over mankind and the jinn." Qatadah, Abu al-Aliyah, al-Rabi' and Ibn Zayd also said: mankind increased in fear and terror of the jinn through this. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means disbelief. There is no doubt that seeking refuge in the jinn instead of seeking refuge in Allah is disbelief and polytheism. It has also been said: the word "men" (rijal) is not applied to the jinn, so the meaning is: there were men among mankind who sought refuge from the evil of the jinn with men among mankind. A man would say, for example: "I seek refuge with Hudhayfah ibn Badr from the jinn of this valley." Al-Qushayri said: this is arbitrary, since it is not far-fetched to apply the word "men" to the jinn.

The Words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And that they thought, as you thought, that Allah would not raise anyone﴾. This is part of the speech of Allah the Exalted addressed to mankind, meaning: and the jinn thought that Allah would not raise up the creation, just as you thought. Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: the jinn thought, just as mankind thought, that Allah would never send a messenger to His creation through whom He would establish proof against them. All of this is a confirmation of the proof against the Quraysh, meaning: if these jinn have believed in Muhammad, then you are more entitled to do so.

Some poet's line: [the poet is Imru' al-Qays; another reading has "*tajawaztu ahrasan ilayha wa mashara*"; the full verse, from his Mu'allaqa, is "*ʿala hirasan law yasharuna maqtali*"] 
(I passed through guards and the terrors of a band of men)

It is also possible that *harasan* is a verbal noun (*masdar*) meaning: it was guarded with a very severe guarding.

*Fa-nqadda ka-l-durri yatba'uhu ... naq'un yathuru takhaluhu tunuba*
(It swooped down like a pearl, followed by a dust cloud that rises; you would think it a tent-peg.)
